title: Iterative Solve
tagline: Find the value of one variable that makes a result -- a variable, a mass or a volume -- hit a target, by re-running a list of features; keep only the answer.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Setting one number so a result comes out right usually means a Pattern 'Reapply features' trick: slow (about 6 % closer per pass) and it keeps every pass. Iterative Solve treats the listed features as a function of the variable, solves for the target and keeps only the accepted trial.
useWhen: A dimension must give a target mass or volume
A variable must make another variable hit a value
Find the first value that meets a condition
slides.caption: Stray_Weight: #flat_length for a target mass -- trial 2 lands on it.

points.head: One trial
points.body: Set the variable, re-run every listed feature under its own id, measure.

points.head: Keep the answer
points.body: Rejected trials are deleted; the accepted one is kept, the originals deleted, the variable set.

points.head: No answer
points.body: An error rolls the whole feature back; the originals stay.

points.head: From the current value
points.body: Current, then +5 %; secant steps; Brent once the target is bracketed.

points.head: Both bounds
points.body: A trial at each bound (they must bracket), then Brent.

points.head: First match
points.body: Even steps from lower to upper; stop at the first value meeting <, <=, > or >=.

items.head: Set the tolerances
items.body: Length tolerance defaults to 25 mm and angle tolerance to 0 (exact).

items.head: Probe first
items.body: Debug > Run once at a value builds one trial without searching.

items.head: Downstream references
items.body: They bind to <solver>trialN<feature> and break if a later edit accepts a different trial.

items.head: Cost
items.body: Every trial re-runs the whole list.
